summary: Verified the new seed_users() ADMIN-rename branch in /app/backend/auth.py. Added /app/backend/tests/test_seed_admin_rename.py (7 async tests using motor rebound to the per-test loop). ALL 7 seed_users behaviors passed: (1) baseline single ADMIN, (2) RENAME in place when ADMIN_EMAIL is fresh and exactly one demo-org ADMIN exists (same id/password_hash/role/organization_id/token_version preserved, count stays 1), (3) EXISTING-EMAIL no-rename/no-duplicate + idempotent, (4) PASSWORD-UPDATE preserved when hash mismatches, (5) GUARD: with >1 ADMINs and a fresh ADMIN_EMAIL the rename does NOT occur (falls back to original insert), (6) 6 demo role users still seeded idempotently, (7) final admin login credentials intact. DB was restored to nelson@patika.dev at the end and ADMIN_EMAIL env restored. Regression: ran test_tugma_backend.py + test_tugma_phase3.py + test_acceptance_iter4.py + test_iter5_role_gate.py -> 50 passed, 3 failed. All 3 failures are in TestEvidenceCompleteness/TestPackage of test_tugma_phase3.py and are PRE-EXISTING DB-state dependencies (no TEST_ evidence rows for the target exception; iteration_5 report itself notes 'evidence records now show 0 for the exception_code query'). They are UNRELATED to the seed_users change — the seed change only touches the users collection.

critical_code_review_comments: seed_users() rename branch is correct and minimally invasive: it only fires when the configured ADMIN_EMAIL is not present AND exactly one demo-org ADMIN exists. All preserved fields (id, password_hash, role, organization_id, token_version) remain untouched because the update sets ONLY 'email'.

One subtle nit: the rename branch does NOT (re)apply the ADMIN_PASSWORD update on the renamed account in the same run — a password rotation combined with an email rename in a single seed_users() invocation will only take effect on the next startup (once the new email exists, the elif password-mismatch branch runs). Not a functional bug for the specified scope, but worth documenting.
auth.py uses os.environ.get('ADMIN_EMAIL', 'admin@example.com') at seeding time — safe default, but consider logging a warning when the default is used in prod.
seed_users() has no protection against a race with itself if called concurrently (two startups) — for a single-instance backend this is fine; document if scaled out.
